$comment: GENERATED by tools/rules-engine from rules/base.rules.yaml and every **/module.rules.yaml. Do not edit.

required.statement: Controllers and endpoints only bind input, call one Application use case and map the result; no business logic, no data access.
Application code depends only on Domain types and ports (interfaces); it never references EF Core, DbContext or infrastructure types.
A module references another module only when listed in its mayDependOn, and never one listed in mustNotDependOn.
Every endpoint has a permission attribute, takes and returns PublicId (never raw database ids), validates its input with a validator and returns errors as problem+json.
Lookup and reference data is created and changed only through EF migrations, never by runtime seeders or manual SQL.

Changes to rules/, packages/, .claude/, the exemptions of any module.rules.yaml, deploy/, .github/, docs/adr/, provenance/, tools/extract/, tools/build.ps1 and the repo-wide build settings need platform-owner review.
Enums are stored and sent as integers and every enum member has an explicit numeric value (Approved = 3), so reordering never changes stored data; labels come from i18n, never from enum names.

Status ids, role keys, permission keys, error codes, config keys, claim types, route names, cache keys, job ids and limits live in typed constants or options classes; numeric literals other than the allowed ones need a named constant.

Use named arguments for non-obvious parameters, small single-purpose methods, guard clauses instead of nesting, meaningful names, and no dead or commented-out code; size and complexity stay within the module thresholds.
Every Application use case, validator, workflow transition, domain rule and Angular service or component with logic ships with unit tests, and each module meets its line-coverage threshold.
Screens are built only from @codelab/ng-dga components and the 8 page patterns.
No user-visible raw text in templates or components; every string is an i18n key present in both ar and en.
Styles use design tokens (CSS variables) and logical properties (inline-start/end) so RTL and LTR both work.

Every route and every action button is gated by a typed permission key (base.fe-routes-gated, base.fe-buttons-gated); the backend endpoint behind it carries [HasPermission] with the same key. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every route that renders a page (component or loadComponent) carries data.permission (RouteDataKeys.Permission, a generated PermissionKeys value) on itself or an ancestor, with permissionGuard() (tagged with Symbol.for('codelab.ng-tools.permission-guard'); an untagged guard fails as missing-guard) on itself or an ancestor, or its full path is in PUBLIC_ROUTE_PATHS (src/app/public-routes.ts); redirects are exempt and every lazily loaded child table is passed to the route-gates spec. Fix: add data: { [RouteDataKeys.Permission]: PermissionKeys.<Key> } or, for a page every visitor may open, the public path. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every action element (a <dga-button>; a <button> with any event binding, a submit button or a typeless one in a submitting form; a role=button element with an event binding; any element binding (click) or (confirm), such as a dialog host) in features/**/*.html and in the inline templates of features/**/*.ts carries *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (on itself, on an ancestor element, or [hasPermission] on an <ng-template> wrapper) or an explicit data-public-action for an action every visitor may take. Fix: add the directive with a generated key, or data-public-action. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

forbidden.description: Reading the system clock directly makes time untestable.
forbidden.fix: Inject TimeProvider and call GetUtcNow() (or GetLocalNow() for display); tests use FakeTimeProvider.

forbidden.description: Thread.Sleep blocks a thread and makes waits untestable; it is also a global banned API (RS0030) in Codelab.Build.Sdk.
forbidden.fix: Use await Task.Delay(delay, timeProvider, cancellationToken) so waits are async and testable.

forbidden.description: The Hangfire dashboard exposes enqueue, delete and requeue of every job behind its own authorization; the starter never maps it.
forbidden.fix: Use the admin Jobs endpoints (jobs.view, jobs.run) and the log.

forbidden.description: Static Hangfire storage hides the database from DI and from tests; the storage comes from the JobStorage singleton of SchedulerRegistration.
forbidden.fix: Resolve JobStorage from DI (SchedulerRegistration.AddJobScheduler registers it).

forbidden.description: Turning off the banned-API, complexity or clean-code (CLB) analyzers removes a build gate for everyone after you (a gate switch set to anything but true, the .NET analyzers or the analysis level off, by id, by a bare pragma, by category severity, by marking code generated, or by relaxing warnings-as-errors). Codelab.Build.Sdk also fails the build (CODELAB002, CODELAB003).
forbidden.fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: An inline suppression (a pragma, with or without a space after the '#'; the SuppressMessage attribute named anywhere, so an alias such as 'using SM = ...SuppressMessageAttribute' is caught too; a unicode escape outside a string or comment, which could spell that name; a NoWarn or WarningsNotAsErrors entry; WarningLevel 0; or a diagnostic severity set to none, silent or suggestion) switches an analyzer off without platform-owner review.
forbidden.fix: Fix the code. A justified suppression is a module.rules.yaml `analyzers` severity (generated into the module .editorconfig) or an `exemptions` entry, both reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: A CodeAnalysisRuleSet, GlobalAnalyzerConfigFiles, EditorConfigFiles, AdditionalFiles or Analyzer item in a project file points the analyzers at configuration (or a suppressor) that no platform owner reviewed, so it can switch any diagnostic off.
forbidden.fix: Remove the item. Analyzer severities and thresholds come from the module.rules.yaml (generated into the module .editorconfig); a new analyzer or analyzer config is a platform-owner change to Codelab.Build.Sdk.

forbidden.description: A .ruleset file can set any diagnostic to Action="None"; the starter configures analyzers only through the rules engine, so no ruleset may exist.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Set analyzer severities in the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: An eslint, stylelint or TypeScript suppression comment (eslint-disable, an inline eslint config, stylelint-disable, @ts-ignore, @ts-nocheck) switches a frontend gate off without platform-owner review.
forbidden.fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: A nested .editorconfig applies to every file below it, so a hand-written one can switch analyzers off or change thresholds for part of a module; the only nested ones are those the rules engine emits at each module root.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Set analyzer severities and thresholds in the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: CodelabFixtureGateOptOut lets a build switch the quality gates off without CODELAB002; only the SDK's own fixture builds may pass it.
forbidden.fix: Remove it. The quality gates stay on for every project; fix the code instead.

forbidden.description: Roslyn loads any .globalconfig it is given, at any global_level, so a hand-written one can raise the clean-code thresholds or switch rules off for a whole project; the only one is the generated rules/codelab.globalconfig.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Change thresholds in rules/base.rules.yaml or a module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: An auto-generated header makes every analyzer skip the file (CLB1001-CLB1005 ignore generated code), so hand-written code must not carry one.
forbidden.fix: Remove the header. Real generator output is written under obj/ by the build and is never committed.

forbidden.description: A *.g.cs, *.generated.cs or *.designer.cs name makes the analyzers treat a hand-written file as generated and skip it.
forbidden.fix: Rename the file to a plain *.cs name. Generator output lives under obj/ and is never committed.

forbidden.description: Only a *.Tests project is a test project (CLB1004 magic numbers skips test projects). Production code may not declare IsTestProject, reference a test framework (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk sets IsTestProject) or rename its assembly to *.Tests.
forbidden.fix: Put tests in a project named <Module>.Tests; production code never declares IsTestProject.

forbidden.description: A certificate validator that accepts everything turns TLS into plain text for an attacker in the path (the harvest source's internal calls did this).
forbidden.fix: Keep certificate validation on. Trust an internal CA through Codelab.Integration's ServerCertificatePolicy (pinned or chain-validated), never by returning true.

forbidden.description: Clean-code thresholds (codelab_* keys) written by hand bypass the rules files and their review; only the files the rules engine emits, at their own paths (rules/codelab.globalconfig and each module's .editorconfig), may set them. A GENERATED marker in the content proves nothing.
forbidden.fix: Change the thresholds or settings in rules/base.rules.yaml or the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: Permission keys passed as string literals drift from the permission catalog.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed permission constant (Permissions.<Area>.<Action> in C#, PermissionKeys.<KEY> in TypeScript).

forbidden.description: Role checks with string literals bypass the permission model.
forbidden.fix: Check a permission with [HasPermission(Permissions.<Area>.<Action>)] instead of a role name.

forbidden.description: Configuration read by string key is untyped and unvalidated.
forbidden.fix: Bind a typed options class with a SectionName constant and ValidateOnStart, then inject IOptions<T>.

forbidden.description: Enums stored or serialized as strings break when a member is renamed.
forbidden.fix: Keep the EF default (int column) and the numeric JSON value; the client maps numbers to i18n labels with the generated TS enum.

forbidden.description: An enum member without an explicit value changes meaning when members are reordered (CLB1005 is the build gate).
forbidden.fix: Give every enum member an explicit numeric value, e.g. Draft = 1, Submitted = 2.

forbidden.description: The Api layer must not touch the database directly.
forbidden.fix: Call an Application use case; only the composition root registers the DbContext.

forbidden.description: Application code must depend on ports, not on EF Core.
forbidden.fix: Declare a port (repository or IUnitOfWork interface) in Application and implement it in Infrastructure.

forbidden.description: Raw numeric or Guid database ids in routes leak internal keys.
forbidden.fix: Take a PublicId route value ({id}) and resolve it in the Application layer.

forbidden.description: An empty catch block hides failures.
forbidden.fix: Handle the error, or let it reach the global exception handler; log with the reference code when you rethrow.

forbidden.description: Commented-out code is dead code; git keeps the history.
forbidden.fix: Delete the commented-out code.

forbidden.description: Feature code must not call HTTP directly.
forbidden.fix: Inject ApiService (or the generated API client) from core/api; it owns the base URL, auth and signing headers.

forbidden.description: Route and API paths typed as literals drift from the route and API catalogs.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed route constants (AppRoutes) and the generated API client instead of path literals.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kits and external DGA packages are not allowed (D5).
forbidden.fix: Use the matching component from @codelab/ng-dga, or ask the platform owner to add one.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kit stylesheets, dependencies (including npm aliases) and angular.json styles/scripts are not allowed (D5).
forbidden.fix: Remove the UI kit's stylesheet, dependency (or its npm alias) or angular.json entry and use @codelab/ng-dga components and tokens, or ask the platform owner to add one.

forbidden.description: Stylesheets imported from a remote URL (CDN) are not allowed (D5, no egress).
forbidden.fix: Install the stylesheet's package through the platform owner (or self-host the asset) and import it locally; UI kits stay refused (D5).

forbidden.description: Shared building blocks (shared/, patterns/, layouts/) must not import feature code.
forbidden.fix: Move what both need into shared/ (or core/), or pass it in through an input; a feature may import shared code, never the reverse.

forbidden.description: Raw text in a template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }}.

forbidden.description: Raw text in an inline component template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }} in the template.

forbidden.description: A permission key written as a string literal in a template gate drifts from the permission catalog (the template check refuses it too).
forbidden.fix: Use the generated key, *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (docs/recipes/add-permission.md).

forbidden.description: Physical left/right properties break RTL.
forbidden.fix: Use logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align start/end).

forbidden.description: Raw colours bypass the design tokens.
forbidden.fix: Use a design token, e.g. var(--codelab-color-primary).

modules.description: Permission catalog (union of every module's IPermissionCatalogSource) synchronized at start, the [HasPermission] handler over a live per-user resolve (direct grants, roles, virtual roles, organization scope), the role and grant editor with the self-lockout guard.

Permissions are resolved live per request from the current rows; never put permission claims in a token and never cache a resolve without invalidating it on every grant change. A grant or role change never bumps the session version.

Every role or grant write passes the ManagerContinuityGuard, so no change leaves zero active non-break-glass users holding both access.roles.manage and access.grants.manage without an explicit break-glass confirmation.

Every endpoint is a thin controller action in Api/ that calls one Application use case, carries [HasPermission] with an AssignmentsPermissionKeys constant and maps the Outcome with OutcomeResults; record ids on the wire are PublicId<QueueRecordIds> (label records) and user ids PublicId<AssigneeUserIds> (label users).

Application code reads and writes data only through ports it declares (IAssignmentStore, IAssigneeEligibility) or kernel ports (IRecordDirectory, IRecordTypeRegistrationSource, IRecordWorkflowCatalogs, IOrganizationScope, IUserDirectory, IAccountAdministration, IRecordSlaReader); the implementations live in Infrastructure or in the module that owns the data.

Every queue read and write opens the queue through RecordQueues, which requires the record type's RecordTypeRegistration.QueuePermissionKey and narrows by its organization scope; a record outside the scope answers 404 RECORDS_NOT_FOUND, exactly like a missing one.

Fix: add the directive with a generated key, or data-public-action. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every endpoint is a thin controller action in Api/ that calls one Application use case, carries [HasPermission] with an AttachmentsPermissionKeys constant and maps the Outcome with OutcomeResults; ids on the wire are PublicId<AttachmentIds> and PublicId<AttachableRecordIds>.

Application code reads and writes data only through ports it declares (IAttachmentStore, IAttachmentReceiptVerifier, IAttachmentStorageClient, IAttachmentFileCleanup, IUploadTicketIssuer); the implementations live in Infrastructure.

Every use case that touches a record's attachments passes AttachableRecords.RefuseAsync (View for list and download, Change for ticket, link and remove) before reading or writing; a missing record and a denied one answer the same 404 (ATTACHMENTS_NOT_FOUND).

A link stores only what IAttachmentReceiptVerifier verified (file id, name, size, SHA-256; MIME type from the extension) after the receipt scope equals UploadScopes.For(record, type, user); never a client-sent hash, size or name.

Attachment types are never edited at run time except IsActive. The Attachments module seeds its own types by migration; a record type's types are declared by the module that owns the record type through Starter.Application.Attachments.IAttachmentTypeSeedSource and written at start by AttachmentTypeSynchronizer (AttachmentTypeSeeding.Plan, matched by key: insert missing, refresh names and rules, never change id, key, record type or IsActive). Every type uses an id from Starter.Domain.Attachments.AttachmentTypeIds and a key from AttachmentTypeKeys, never reused, and its extensions stay inside Codelab:Security:Uploads AllowedExtensions (checked at start).
A removal is soft and saved first; the deletion of the bytes is enqueued afterwards through IAttachmentFileCleanup (outbox type attachments.delete-file), never called inline.

Every route and every action button is gated by a typed permission key (base.fe-routes-gated, base.fe-buttons-gated); the backend endpoint behind it carries [HasPermission] with the same key. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Fix: add data: { [RouteDataKeys.Permission]: PermissionKeys.<Key> } or, for a page every visitor may open, the public path. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every action element (a <dga-button>; a <button> with any event binding, a submit button or a typeless one in a submitting form; a role=button element with an event binding; any element binding (click) or (confirm), such as a dialog host) in features/**/*.html and in the inline templates of features/**/*.ts carries *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (on itself, on an ancestor element, or [hasPermission] on an <ng-template> wrapper) or an explicit data-public-action for an action every visitor may take. Fix: add the directive with a generated key, or data-public-action. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Domain references nothing outside itself; Application references Domain and the kernel ports only (no EF Core, no ASP.NET Core, no Codelab.Security); Infrastructure holds EF Core, JWT and the security-store adapters; Api holds thin controllers that call one use case each.
Every access and refresh token is issued by SessionIssuer (through SessionTokens); no other code signs a token or writes a session.
Access tokens carry identity and session claims only (sub, sid, sver, skid, jti); never a permission or role claim. Permissions are resolved live by the Access module.
Identity never references the Access module. Grants go through IUserPermissionGrants; the keys a Development user receives are constants of DevUserPermissionKeys.

Deactivation, an activation link (password reset), an activation redemption, a binding change and a rotated configured password bump the user's session version before the change is saved (AccountWrites.SaveAsync with SessionImpact.EndSessions); grant and role changes never bump (permissions are live).
Auth events store no password, token, ticket or raw user name: the typed identifier only as its keyed UserIdHash, the user only as the internal id. The sink never throws (except cancellation).

forbidden.description: Turning off the banned-API, complexity or clean-code (CLB) analyzers removes a build gate for everyone after you (a gate switch set to anything but true, the .NET analyzers or the analysis level off, by id, by a bare pragma, by category severity, by marking code generated, or by relaxing warnings-as-errors). forbidden.description: A CodeAnalysisRuleSet, GlobalAnalyzerConfigFiles, EditorConfigFiles, AdditionalFiles or Analyzer item in a project file points the analyzers at configuration (or a suppressor) that no platform owner reviewed, so it can switch any diagnostic off.

forbidden.description: A .ruleset file can set any diagnostic to Action="None"; the starter configures analyzers only through the rules engine, so no ruleset may exist.

forbidden.description: An eslint, stylelint or TypeScript suppression comment (eslint-disable, an inline eslint config, stylelint-disable, @ts-ignore, @ts-nocheck) switches a frontend gate off without platform-owner review.
forbidden.fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: A nested .editorconfig applies to every file below it, so a hand-written one can switch analyzers off or change thresholds for part of a module; the only nested ones are those the rules engine emits at each module root.

forbidden.description: CodelabFixtureGateOptOut lets a build switch the quality gates off without CODELAB002; only the SDK's own fixture builds may pass it.

forbidden.description: An auto-generated header makes every analyzer skip the file (CLB1001-CLB1005 ignore generated code), so hand-written code must not carry one.
forbidden.fix: Remove the header. Real generator output is written under obj/ by the build and is never committed.

forbidden.description: A *.g.cs, *.generated.cs or *.designer.cs name makes the analyzers treat a hand-written file as generated and skip it.

forbidden.description: Only a *.Tests project is a test project (CLB1004 magic numbers skips test projects). Production code may not declare IsTestProject, reference a test framework (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk sets IsTestProject) or rename its assembly to *.Tests.

forbidden.description: A certificate validator that accepts everything turns TLS into plain text for an attacker in the path (the harvest source's internal calls did this).

forbidden.description: Clean-code thresholds (codelab_* keys) written by hand bypass the rules files and their review; only the files the rules engine emits, at their own paths (rules/codelab.globalconfig and each module's .editorconfig), may set them. forbidden.fix: Change the thresholds or settings in rules/base.rules.yaml or the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.fix: Call an Application use case; only the composition root registers the DbContext.

forbidden.description: Commented-out code is dead code; git keeps the history.

forbidden.description: Feature code must not call HTTP directly.

forbidden.description: Route and API paths typed as literals drift from the route and API catalogs.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kits and external DGA packages are not allowed (D5).

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kit stylesheets, dependencies (including npm aliases) and angular.json styles/scripts are not allowed (D5).

forbidden.description: Shared building blocks (shared/, patterns/, layouts/) must not import feature code.

forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }} in the template.

forbidden.fix: Use the generated key, *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (docs/recipes/add-permission.md).

forbidden.description: Physical left/right properties break RTL.
forbidden.fix: Use logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align start/end).

forbidden.description: Raw colours bypass the design tokens.

modules.description: Background jobs (module 6b): the catalog of every IJob a module registers with AddStarterJob, the run history in schema jobs (actor SYSTEM), manual runs and recurring schedules on Hangfire (schema hangfire, no dashboard, a job server per node behind Jobs:Enabled), and the built-in outbox-drain and security-replay-purge jobs.

required.statement: Controllers and endpoints only bind input, call one Application use case and map the result; no business logic, no data access.

Every endpoint has a permission attribute, takes and returns PublicId (never raw database ids), validates its input with a validator and returns errors as problem+json.
Lookup and reference data is created and changed only through EF migrations, never by runtime seeders or manual SQL.

Fix: add the directive with a generated key, or data-public-action. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every endpoint is a thin controller action in Api/ that calls one Application use case, carries [HasPermission] with a JobsPermissionKeys constant and maps the Outcome with OutcomeResults (or JobsResults for 202).

Every run executes inside ISystemActorScope and is recorded with the actor SystemActor.Name; a job never acts as a user account or a role, and the administrator who triggers a run is recorded only as TriggeredBy.
A failed run stores only the classified code (IFailureCodeResolver) and its reference code, never an exception message or stack trace; the exception goes to the one log line.
Hangfire types appear only in Infrastructure/Scheduling; Application sees the IJobQueue and IJobRunLock ports and the kernel IJob.
The Hangfire dashboard is never mapped; operators read runs on the admin Jobs screen and failures in the log.

required.statement: Controllers and endpoints only bind input, call one Application use case and map the result; no business logic, no data access.
Application code depends only on Domain types and ports (interfaces); it never references EF Core, DbContext or infrastructure types.
A module references another module only when listed in its mayDependOn, and never one listed in mustNotDependOn.
Every endpoint has a permission attribute, takes and returns PublicId (never raw database ids), validates its input with a validator and returns errors as problem+json.
Lookup and reference data is created and changed only through EF migrations, never by runtime seeders or manual SQL.

Every Application use case, validator, workflow transition, domain rule and Angular service or component with logic ships with unit tests, and each module meets its line-coverage threshold.
Screens are built only from @codelab/ng-dga components and the 8 page patterns.
No user-visible raw text in templates or components; every string is an i18n key present in both ar and en.
Styles use design tokens (CSS variables) and logical properties (inline-start/end) so RTL and LTR both work.

Every route and every action button is gated by a typed permission key (base.fe-routes-gated, base.fe-buttons-gated); the backend endpoint behind it carries [HasPermission] with the same key. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every route that renders a page (component or loadComponent) carries data.permission (RouteDataKeys.Permission, a generated PermissionKeys value) on itself or an ancestor, with permissionGuard() (tagged with Symbol.for('codelab.ng-tools.permission-guard'); an untagged guard fails as missing-guard) on itself or an ancestor, or its full path is in PUBLIC_ROUTE_PATHS (src/app/public-routes.ts); redirects are exempt and every lazily loaded child table is passed to the route-gates spec. Fix: add data: { [RouteDataKeys.Permission]: PermissionKeys.<Key> } or, for a page every visitor may open, the public path. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every action element (a <dga-button>; a <button> with any event binding, a submit button or a typeless one in a submitting form; a role=button element with an event binding; any element binding (click) or (confirm), such as a dialog host) in features/**/*.html and in the inline templates of features/**/*.ts carries *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (on itself, on an ancestor element, or [hasPermission] on an <ng-template> wrapper) or an explicit data-public-action for an action every visitor may take. Fix: add the directive with a generated key, or data-public-action. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every endpoint is a thin controller action in Api/ that calls one Application use case, carries [HasPermission] with a NotificationsPermissionKeys constant (or [AuthenticatedUser] for the caller's own feed, allowlisted) and maps the Outcome with OutcomeResults.
Application code reads and writes data only through ports it declares (INotificationStore, ITemplateStore, IEmailSender, ISmsSender); the implementations live in Infrastructure.
Template texts are inserted and changed only by Notifications migrations, Arabic and English for every channel a key is sent on; nothing writes NotificationTemplates at run time.

Every text is rendered by TemplateRenderer; a placeholder without a value refuses the send (NOTIFICATIONS_PLACEHOLDER_MISSING), so a raw {{token}} never reaches a recipient. E-mail bodies HTML-encode every value; subjects and titles are one line.

Outbox payloads carry only the notification id and channel. A secret-bearing link (activation) is sent with SendImmediateEmailAsync from an outbox handler and never stored; logs carry ids only, never addresses, placeholder values or texts.
An outbox handler sends a channel only while its state is Pending and records Sent (or NoAddress) right after, so a re-delivered outbox message is not sent twice once recorded.

E-mail goes only to the SMTP relay inside the backend zone or the pickup folder; SMS only to the file sink or the integration gateway SMS relay (GatewaySmsSender). No sender calls an internet host (decision D2).

Every endpoint is a thin action of OpsController under OpsRoutes.Root, authorized only by [OpsServiceCaller] (the Codelab.Security service-assertion scheme plus the trusted-caller requirement); never [HasPermission], [AllowAnonymous], [AuthenticatedUser], [SignatureExempt] or a second scheme (JWT, cookie, API key).

Every Ops action carries [OpsEndpoint] and runs behind OperatorAccessFilter, which refuses a call without the X-Codelab-Operator header (400 OPS_OPERATOR_REQUIRED) and records the operator in ops.OperatorAccess.

Health components and certificate rows carry only OpsFindingCodes constants, never an exception message, a host name or a URL; failure logs carry identifiers only (endpoint, correlation id, counts), never the operator name.

forbidden.description: CodelabFixtureGateOptOut lets a build switch the quality gates off without CODELAB002; only the SDK's own fixture builds may pass it.

forbidden.description: Only a *.Tests project is a test project (CLB1004 magic numbers skips test projects). Production code may not declare IsTestProject, reference a test framework (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk sets IsTestProject) or rename its assembly to *.Tests.

forbidden.description: A certificate validator that accepts everything turns TLS into plain text for an attacker in the path (the harvest source's internal calls did this).

forbidden.description: Clean-code thresholds (codelab_* keys) written by hand bypass the rules files and their review; only the files the rules engine emits, at their own paths (rules/codelab.globalconfig and each module's .editorconfig), may set them. forbidden.fix: Give every enum member an explicit numeric value, e.g. Draft = 1, Submitted = 2.

forbidden.description: The Api layer must not touch the database directly.
forbidden.fix: Call an Application use case; only the composition root registers the DbContext.

forbidden.description: Application code must depend on ports, not on EF Core.

forbidden.description: Commented-out code is dead code; git keeps the history.
forbidden.fix: Delete the commented-out code.

forbidden.description: Feature code must not call HTTP directly.
forbidden.fix: Inject ApiService (or the generated API client) from core/api; it owns the base URL, auth and signing headers.

forbidden.description: Route and API paths typed as literals drift from the route and API catalogs.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed route constants (AppRoutes) and the generated API client instead of path literals.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kits and external DGA packages are not allowed (D5).
forbidden.fix: Use the matching component from @codelab/ng-dga, or ask the platform owner to add one.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kit stylesheets, dependencies (including npm aliases) and angular.json styles/scripts are not allowed (D5).
forbidden.fix: Remove the UI kit's stylesheet, dependency (or its npm alias) or angular.json entry and use @codelab/ng-dga components and tokens, or ask the platform owner to add one.

forbidden.description: Stylesheets imported from a remote URL (CDN) are not allowed (D5, no egress).

forbidden.description: Shared building blocks (shared/, patterns/, layouts/) must not import feature code.
forbidden.fix: Move what both need into shared/ (or core/), or pass it in through an input; a feature may import shared code, never the reverse.

forbidden.description: Raw text in a template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }}.

forbidden.description: Raw text in an inline component template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }} in the template.

forbidden.description: A permission key written as a string literal in a template gate drifts from the permission catalog (the template check refuses it too).
forbidden.fix: Use the generated key, *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (docs/recipes/add-permission.md).

forbidden.description: Physical left/right properties break RTL.
forbidden.fix: Use logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align start/end).

forbidden.description: Raw colours bypass the design tokens.
forbidden.fix: Use a design token, e.g. var(--codelab-color-primary).

forbidden.description: The Ops module reads other modules only through kernel ports (IJob registrations, IJobRunHistory and IIdentityProviderKeySet); a module reference couples them and breaks removing either one.

forbidden.description: Accepting any server certificate hides the very TLS failures the Ops surface exists to show.
forbidden.fix: Trust the issuing CA on the server instead; the probe reports OPS_PROBE_UNREACHABLE until it is trusted.

modules.description: Public portal backend (module 15): the anonymous, rate-limited contact form (CU-YYYY-NNN reference number, stored in schema portal, announced to the configured inbox through the Notifications kernel port) and the bilingual FAQ, service guide, privacy and terms content (seeded by migration, cached public read, admin replace).

required.statement: Controllers and endpoints only bind input, call one Application use case and map the result; no business logic, no data access.
Application code depends only on Domain types and ports (interfaces); it never references EF Core, DbContext or infrastructure types.
A module references another module only when listed in its mayDependOn, and never one listed in mustNotDependOn.
Every endpoint has a permission attribute, takes and returns PublicId (never raw database ids), validates its input with a validator and returns errors as problem+json.
Lookup and reference data is created and changed only through EF migrations, never by runtime seeders or manual SQL.

Changes to rules/, packages/, .claude/, the exemptions of any module.rules.yaml, deploy/, .github/, docs/adr/, provenance/, tools/extract/, tools/build.ps1 and the repo-wide build settings need platform-owner review.
Enums are stored and sent as integers and every enum member has an explicit numeric value (Approved = 3), so reordering never changes stored data; labels come from i18n, never from enum names.

Status ids, role keys, permission keys, error codes, config keys, claim types, route names, cache keys, job ids and limits live in typed constants or options classes; numeric literals other than the allowed ones need a named constant.

Use named arguments for non-obvious parameters, small single-purpose methods, guard clauses instead of nesting, meaningful names, and no dead or commented-out code; size and complexity stay within the module thresholds.
Every Application use case, validator, workflow transition, domain rule and Angular service or component with logic ships with unit tests, and each module meets its line-coverage threshold.
Screens are built only from @codelab/ng-dga components and the 8 page patterns.
No user-visible raw text in templates or components; every string is an i18n key present in both ar and en.
Styles use design tokens (CSS variables) and logical properties (inline-start/end) so RTL and LTR both work.

Every route and every action button is gated by a typed permission key (base.fe-routes-gated, base.fe-buttons-gated); the backend endpoint behind it carries [HasPermission] with the same key. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every route that renders a page (component or loadComponent) carries data.permission (RouteDataKeys.Permission, a generated PermissionKeys value) on itself or an ancestor, with permissionGuard() (tagged with Symbol.for('codelab.ng-tools.permission-guard'); an untagged guard fails as missing-guard) on itself or an ancestor, or its full path is in PUBLIC_ROUTE_PATHS (src/app/public-routes.ts); redirects are exempt and every lazily loaded child table is passed to the route-gates spec. Fix: add the directive with a generated key, or data-public-action. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every endpoint is a thin controller action in Api/ that calls one Application use case and maps its Outcome with OutcomeResults or PortalResults; admin endpoints carry [HasPermission] with a PortalPermissionKeys constant, the two public ones [AllowAnonymous] and an EndpointAllowlist entry.

The contact form is the module's only anonymous write and carries [EnableRateLimiting(ClientRateLimitOptions.PolicyName)] (the per-client, trusted-proxy aware policy); no Portal endpoint disables rate limiting.

A contact message is validated, numbered (IRequestNumberAllocator, PortalNumberPrefixes.ContactUs) and saved before the inbox is notified; a notification failure after the save is logged with the reference number only and never turns the stored message into an error.

Every ContactMessage column that holds what the sender typed (name, e-mail, message) carries [PersonalData], so the audit trail keeps only the masked form; logs carry the reference number, never the sender's details.
Section titles and bodies are plain text (paragraphs separated by a blank line), never HTML or Markdown; the client renders them as text.
A content replace that changes anything drops that page's cached public content after the save; no cache entry outlives PortalLimits.ContentCacheTtl.
Application code reads and writes data only through ports it declares (IContactMessageStore, IPortalContentStore, IContactTopics, IPortalContentCache); the implementations live in Infrastructure.

Fix: add the directive with a generated key, or data-public-action. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every endpoint is a thin controller action in Api/ that calls one Application use case and maps the Outcome with OutcomeResults; ids on the wire are PublicId<RecordsIds>. The oversight list carries [HasPermission(RecordsPermissionKeys.OversightView)]; the per-record-type endpoints carry [AuthenticatedUser] (allowlisted) because their permissions come from the record type's registration and catalog, and every use case checks them live through RecordLoader / RecordStandings.
Application code reads and writes data only through IRecordStore; the EF implementation lives in Infrastructure.

Every transition goes through RecordWorkflowEngine.Decide (refusals mapped once by WorkflowRefusals.ToRefusal) and every offered action comes from RecordWorkflowEngine.AllowedActions; no status matrix, no switch on a status or an action key outside RecordLifecycleActions.

Submit and resubmit (also through the generic transitions endpoint) run every IRecordSubmitValidator of the record type, then RequiredAttachmentsGate.RefuseWhileMissingAsync, and only then take the number with IRequestNumberAllocator; refusals map through SubmitRefusals / WorkflowRefusals, never a per-controller switch.

The status change and its RecordHistory row are saved in one transaction (RecordCommits, IRecordStore.AddDraftAsync); RecordHistory is mapped with HasRecordHistory (ON DELETE RESTRICT) and is never updated or deleted.
Transition observers and notifications run after the commit, each in its own catch (ERROR-HANDLING row 8) that logs identifiers only; a failure never undoes or fails the committed transition.

Every endpoint is a thin controller action in Api/ that calls one Application use case, carries [HasPermission] with a ServiceRequestsPermissionKeys constant (or [AuthenticatedUser] with the access check in the use case and an EndpointAllowlist entry) and maps the Outcome with OutcomeResults or ServiceRequestsResults.

Who may see a service request, its details and its files is decided only by the Records module (IRecordVisibility and the attachable access it publishes through IAttachableRecordAccessSource); ServiceRequestAccess adds only the owner check of the draft endpoints and never decides visibility itself.

forbidden.description: Commented-out code is dead code; git keeps the history.

forbidden.description: Physical left/right properties break RTL.

forbidden.description: Raw colours bypass the design tokens.

Accounts are read and changed only through the kernel IAccountAdministration port (implemented by Identity); the Users module never references the Identity or Access module, their tables or their types.

Every action element (a <dga-button>; a <button> with any event binding, a submit button or a typeless one in a submitting form; a role=button element with an event binding; any element binding (click) or (confirm), such as a dialog host) in features/**/*.html and in the inline templates of features/**/*.ts carries *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (on itself, on an ancestor element, or [hasPermission] on an <ng-template> wrapper) or an explicit data-public-action for an action every visitor may take. Fix: add the directive with a generated key, or data-public-action. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.
Program.cs stays at 150 lines or fewer and names no module; new wiring goes into a kernel or module Add/Use extension.
Modules are listed only as ProjectReferences in Starter.Api.csproj, added by tools/scaffold/new-module.mjs and removed by tools/remove-module.ps1.

forbidden.description: Reading the system clock directly makes time untestable.
forbidden.fix: Inject TimeProvider and call GetUtcNow() (or GetLocalNow() for display); tests use FakeTimeProvider.

forbidden.description: Thread.Sleep blocks a thread and makes waits untestable; it is also a global banned API (RS0030) in Codelab.Build.Sdk.
forbidden.fix: Use await Task.Delay(delay, timeProvider, cancellationToken) so waits are async and testable.

forbidden.description: The Hangfire dashboard exposes enqueue, delete and requeue of every job behind its own authorization; the starter never maps it.
forbidden.fix: Use the admin Jobs endpoints (jobs.view, jobs.run) and the log.

forbidden.description: Static Hangfire storage hides the database from DI and from tests; the storage comes from the JobStorage singleton of SchedulerRegistration.
forbidden.fix: Resolve JobStorage from DI (SchedulerRegistration.AddJobScheduler registers it).

forbidden.description: Turning off the banned-API, complexity or clean-code (CLB) analyzers removes a build gate for everyone after you (a gate switch set to anything but true, the .NET analyzers or the analysis level off, by id, by a bare pragma, by category severity, by marking code generated, or by relaxing warnings-as-errors). Codelab.Build.Sdk also fails the build (CODELAB002, CODELAB003).
forbidden.fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: An inline suppression (a pragma, with or without a space after the '#'; the SuppressMessage attribute named anywhere, so an alias such as 'using SM = ...SuppressMessageAttribute' is caught too; a unicode escape outside a string or comment, which could spell that name; a NoWarn or WarningsNotAsErrors entry; WarningLevel 0; or a diagnostic severity set to none, silent or suggestion) switches an analyzer off without platform-owner review.
forbidden.fix: Fix the code. A justified suppression is a module.rules.yaml `analyzers` severity (generated into the module .editorconfig) or an `exemptions` entry, both reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: A CodeAnalysisRuleSet, GlobalAnalyzerConfigFiles, EditorConfigFiles, AdditionalFiles or Analyzer item in a project file points the analyzers at configuration (or a suppressor) that no platform owner reviewed, so it can switch any diagnostic off.
forbidden.fix: Remove the item. Analyzer severities and thresholds come from the module.rules.yaml (generated into the module .editorconfig); a new analyzer or analyzer config is a platform-owner change to Codelab.Build.Sdk.

forbidden.description: A .ruleset file can set any diagnostic to Action="None"; the starter configures analyzers only through the rules engine, so no ruleset may exist.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Set analyzer severities in the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: An eslint, stylelint or TypeScript suppression comment (eslint-disable, an inline eslint config, stylelint-disable, @ts-ignore, @ts-nocheck) switches a frontend gate off without platform-owner review.
forbidden.fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: A nested .editorconfig applies to every file below it, so a hand-written one can switch analyzers off or change thresholds for part of a module; the only nested ones are those the rules engine emits at each module root.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Set analyzer severities and thresholds in the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: CodelabFixtureGateOptOut lets a build switch the quality gates off without CODELAB002; only the SDK's own fixture builds may pass it.
forbidden.fix: Remove it. The quality gates stay on for every project; fix the code instead.

forbidden.description: Roslyn loads any .globalconfig it is given, at any global_level, so a hand-written one can raise the clean-code thresholds or switch rules off for a whole project; the only one is the generated rules/codelab.globalconfig.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Change thresholds in rules/base.rules.yaml or a module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: An auto-generated header makes every analyzer skip the file (CLB1001-CLB1005 ignore generated code), so hand-written code must not carry one.
forbidden.fix: Remove the header. Real generator output is written under obj/ by the build and is never committed.

forbidden.description: A *.g.cs, *.generated.cs or *.designer.cs name makes the analyzers treat a hand-written file as generated and skip it.
forbidden.fix: Rename the file to a plain *.cs name. Generator output lives under obj/ and is never committed.

forbidden.description: Only a *.Tests project is a test project (CLB1004 magic numbers skips test projects). Production code may not declare IsTestProject, reference a test framework (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk sets IsTestProject) or rename its assembly to *.Tests.
forbidden.fix: Put tests in a project named <Module>.Tests; production code never declares IsTestProject.

forbidden.description: A certificate validator that accepts everything turns TLS into plain text for an attacker in the path (the harvest source's internal calls did this).
forbidden.fix: Keep certificate validation on. Trust an internal CA through Codelab.Integration's ServerCertificatePolicy (pinned or chain-validated), never by returning true.

forbidden.description: Clean-code thresholds (codelab_* keys) written by hand bypass the rules files and their review; only the files the rules engine emits, at their own paths (rules/codelab.globalconfig and each module's .editorconfig), may set them. A GENERATED marker in the content proves nothing.
forbidden.fix: Change the thresholds or settings in rules/base.rules.yaml or the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: Permission keys passed as string literals drift from the permission catalog.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed permission constant (Permissions.<Area>.<Action> in C#, PermissionKeys.<KEY> in TypeScript).

forbidden.description: Role checks with string literals bypass the permission model.
forbidden.fix: Check a permission with [HasPermission(Permissions.<Area>.<Action>)] instead of a role name.

forbidden.description: Configuration read by string key is untyped and unvalidated.
forbidden.fix: Bind a typed options class with a SectionName constant and ValidateOnStart, then inject IOptions<T>.

forbidden.description: Enums stored or serialized as strings break when a member is renamed.
forbidden.fix: Keep the EF default (int column) and the numeric JSON value; the client maps numbers to i18n labels with the generated TS enum.

forbidden.description: An enum member without an explicit value changes meaning when members are reordered (CLB1005 is the build gate).
forbidden.fix: Give every enum member an explicit numeric value, e.g. Draft = 1, Submitted = 2.

forbidden.description: The Api layer must not touch the database directly.
forbidden.fix: Call an Application use case; only the composition root registers the DbContext.

forbidden.description: Application code must depend on ports, not on EF Core.
forbidden.fix: Declare a port (repository or IUnitOfWork interface) in Application and implement it in Infrastructure.

forbidden.description: Raw numeric or Guid database ids in routes leak internal keys.
forbidden.fix: Take a PublicId route value ({id}) and resolve it in the Application layer.

forbidden.description: An empty catch block hides failures.
forbidden.fix: Handle the error, or let it reach the global exception handler; log with the reference code when you rethrow.

forbidden.description: Commented-out code is dead code; git keeps the history.
forbidden.fix: Delete the commented-out code.

forbidden.description: Feature code must not call HTTP directly.
forbidden.fix: Inject ApiService (or the generated API client) from core/api; it owns the base URL, auth and signing headers.

forbidden.description: Route and API paths typed as literals drift from the route and API catalogs.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed route constants (AppRoutes) and the generated API client instead of path literals.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kits and external DGA packages are not allowed (D5).
forbidden.fix: Use the matching component from @codelab/ng-dga, or ask the platform owner to add one.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kit stylesheets, dependencies (including npm aliases) and angular.json styles/scripts are not allowed (D5).
forbidden.fix: Remove the UI kit's stylesheet, dependency (or its npm alias) or angular.json entry and use @codelab/ng-dga components and tokens, or ask the platform owner to add one.

forbidden.description: Stylesheets imported from a remote URL (CDN) are not allowed (D5, no egress).
forbidden.fix: Install the stylesheet's package through the platform owner (or self-host the asset) and import it locally; UI kits stay refused (D5).

forbidden.description: Shared building blocks (shared/, patterns/, layouts/) must not import feature code.
forbidden.fix: Move what both need into shared/ (or core/), or pass it in through an input; a feature may import shared code, never the reverse.

forbidden.description: Raw text in a template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }}.

forbidden.description: Raw text in an inline component template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }} in the template.

forbidden.description: A permission key written as a string literal in a template gate drifts from the permission catalog (the template check refuses it too).
forbidden.fix: Use the generated key, *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (docs/recipes/add-permission.md).

forbidden.description: Physical left/right properties break RTL.
forbidden.fix: Use logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align start/end).

forbidden.description: Raw colours bypass the design tokens.
forbidden.fix: Use a design token, e.g. var(--codelab-color-primary).

forbidden.description: The host never uses a module's types; it only references the module projects for discovery.
forbidden.fix: Put the wiring in the module's Add/Use extension, called through its IModule.

modules.description: Kernel Application: ports only (persistence, language, current user, audit, permission catalog and grants, user directory, validator) and the use-case result types (Outcome, Refusal).

forbidden.fix: Fix the code. A justified suppression is a module.rules.yaml `analyzers` severity (generated into the module .editorconfig) or an `exemptions` entry, both reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: A CodeAnalysisRuleSet, GlobalAnalyzerConfigFiles, EditorConfigFiles, AdditionalFiles or Analyzer item in a project file points the analyzers at configuration (or a suppressor) that no platform owner reviewed, so it can switch any diagnostic off.
forbidden.fix: Remove the item. Analyzer severities and thresholds come from the module.rules.yaml (generated into the module .editorconfig); a new analyzer or analyzer config is a platform-owner change to Codelab.Build.Sdk.

forbidden.description: A .ruleset file can set any diagnostic to Action="None"; the starter configures analyzers only through the rules engine, so no ruleset may exist.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Set analyzer severities in the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: An eslint, stylelint or TypeScript suppression comment (eslint-disable, an inline eslint config, stylelint-disable, @ts-ignore, @ts-nocheck) switches a frontend gate off without platform-owner review.
forbidden.fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: A nested .editorconfig applies to every file below it, so a hand-written one can switch analyzers off or change thresholds for part of a module; the only nested ones are those the rules engine emits at each module root.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Set analyzer severities and thresholds in the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: CodelabFixtureGateOptOut lets a build switch the quality gates off without CODELAB002; only the SDK's own fixture builds may pass it.
forbidden.fix: Remove it. The quality gates stay on for every project; fix the code instead.

forbidden.description: Roslyn loads any .globalconfig it is given, at any global_level, so a hand-written one can raise the clean-code thresholds or switch rules off for a whole project; the only one is the generated rules/codelab.globalconfig.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Change thresholds in rules/base.rules.yaml or a module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: An auto-generated header makes every analyzer skip the file (CLB1001-CLB1005 ignore generated code), so hand-written code must not carry one.
forbidden.fix: Remove the header. Real generator output is written under obj/ by the build and is never committed.

forbidden.description: A *.g.cs, *.generated.cs or *.designer.cs name makes the analyzers treat a hand-written file as generated and skip it.
forbidden.fix: Rename the file to a plain *.cs name. Generator output lives under obj/ and is never committed.

forbidden.description: Only a *.Tests project is a test project (CLB1004 magic numbers skips test projects). Production code may not declare IsTestProject, reference a test framework (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk sets IsTestProject) or rename its assembly to *.Tests.
forbidden.fix: Put tests in a project named <Module>.Tests; production code never declares IsTestProject.

forbidden.description: A certificate validator that accepts everything turns TLS into plain text for an attacker in the path (the harvest source's internal calls did this).
forbidden.fix: Keep certificate validation on. Trust an internal CA through Codelab.Integration's ServerCertificatePolicy (pinned or chain-validated), never by returning true.

forbidden.description: Clean-code thresholds (codelab_* keys) written by hand bypass the rules files and their review; only the files the rules engine emits, at their own paths (rules/codelab.globalconfig and each module's .editorconfig), may set them. A GENERATED marker in the content proves nothing.
forbidden.fix: Change the thresholds or settings in rules/base.rules.yaml or the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: Permission keys passed as string literals drift from the permission catalog.

forbidden.description: Role checks with string literals bypass the permission model.
forbidden.fix: Check a permission with [HasPermission(Permissions.<Area>.<Action>)] instead of a role name.

forbidden.description: Configuration read by string key is untyped and unvalidated.
forbidden.fix: Bind a typed options class with a SectionName constant and ValidateOnStart, then inject IOptions<T>.

forbidden.description: Enums stored or serialized as strings break when a member is renamed.
forbidden.fix: Keep the EF default (int column) and the numeric JSON value; the client maps numbers to i18n labels with the generated TS enum.

forbidden.description: An enum member without an explicit value changes meaning when members are reordered (CLB1005 is the build gate).
forbidden.fix: Give every enum member an explicit numeric value, e.g. Draft = 1, Submitted = 2.

forbidden.description: The Api layer must not touch the database directly.
forbidden.fix: Call an Application use case; only the composition root registers the DbContext.

forbidden.description: Application code must depend on ports, not on EF Core.
forbidden.fix: Declare a port (repository or IUnitOfWork interface) in Application and implement it in Infrastructure.

forbidden.description: Raw numeric or Guid database ids in routes leak internal keys.
forbidden.fix: Take a PublicId route value ({id}) and resolve it in the Application layer.

forbidden.description: An empty catch block hides failures.
forbidden.fix: Handle the error, or let it reach the global exception handler; log with the reference code when you rethrow.

forbidden.description: Commented-out code is dead code; git keeps the history.
forbidden.fix: Delete the commented-out code.

forbidden.description: Feature code must not call HTTP directly.
forbidden.fix: Inject ApiService (or the generated API client) from core/api; it owns the base URL, auth and signing headers.

forbidden.description: Route and API paths typed as literals drift from the route and API catalogs.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed route constants (AppRoutes) and the generated API client instead of path literals.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kits and external DGA packages are not allowed (D5).
forbidden.fix: Use the matching component from @codelab/ng-dga, or ask the platform owner to add one.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kit stylesheets, dependencies (including npm aliases) and angular.json styles/scripts are not allowed (D5).

forbidden.description: Stylesheets imported from a remote URL (CDN) are not allowed (D5, no egress).
forbidden.fix: Install the stylesheet's package through the platform owner (or self-host the asset) and import it locally; UI kits stay refused (D5).

forbidden.description: Shared building blocks (shared/, patterns/, layouts/) must not import feature code.
forbidden.fix: Move what both need into shared/ (or core/), or pass it in through an input; a feature may import shared code, never the reverse.

forbidden.description: Raw text in a template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }}.

forbidden.description: Raw text in an inline component template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }} in the template.

forbidden.description: A permission key written as a string literal in a template gate drifts from the permission catalog (the template check refuses it too).
forbidden.fix: Use the generated key, *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (docs/recipes/add-permission.md).

forbidden.description: Physical left/right properties break RTL.
forbidden.fix: Use logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align start/end).

forbidden.description: Raw colours bypass the design tokens.
forbidden.fix: Use a design token, e.g. var(--codelab-color-primary).

forbidden.description: The kernel Domain is plain .NET; frameworks and Codelab packages belong to Infrastructure.
forbidden.fix: Move the code that needs the framework to Starter.Infrastructure, behind a port in Starter.Application.

modules.description: Kernel Infrastructure: module discovery and registration, the module DbContext base and startup runner, authorization defaults, feature switches, HTTP adapters of the kernel ports, refusal and exception mapping, the request pipeline.

required.statement: Controllers and endpoints only bind input, call one Application use case and map the result; no business logic, no data access.
Application code depends only on Domain types and ports (interfaces); it never references EF Core, DbContext or infrastructure types.
A module references another module only when listed in its mayDependOn, and never one listed in mustNotDependOn.
Every endpoint has a permission attribute, takes and returns PublicId (never raw database ids), validates its input with a validator and returns errors as problem+json.
Lookup and reference data is created and changed only through EF migrations, never by runtime seeders or manual SQL.

Changes to rules/, packages/, .claude/, the exemptions of any module.rules.yaml, deploy/, .github/, docs/adr/, provenance/, tools/extract/, tools/build.ps1 and the repo-wide build settings need platform-owner review.
Enums are stored and sent as integers and every enum member has an explicit numeric value (Approved = 3), so reordering never changes stored data; labels come from i18n, never from enum names.

Status ids, role keys, permission keys, error codes, config keys, claim types, route names, cache keys, job ids and limits live in typed constants or options classes; numeric literals other than the allowed ones need a named constant.

Use named arguments for non-obvious parameters, small single-purpose methods, guard clauses instead of nesting, meaningful names, and no dead or commented-out code; size and complexity stay within the module thresholds.
Every Application use case, validator, workflow transition, domain rule and Angular service or component with logic ships with unit tests, and each module meets its line-coverage threshold.
Screens are built only from @codelab/ng-dga components and the 8 page patterns.
No user-visible raw text in templates or components; every string is an i18n key present in both ar and en.
Styles use design tokens (CSS variables) and logical properties (inline-start/end) so RTL and LTR both work.

Every route and every action button is gated by a typed permission key (base.fe-routes-gated, base.fe-buttons-gated); the backend endpoint behind it carries [HasPermission] with the same key. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every route that renders a page (component or loadComponent) carries data.permission (RouteDataKeys.Permission, a generated PermissionKeys value) on itself or an ancestor, with permissionGuard() (tagged with Symbol.for('codelab.ng-tools.permission-guard'); an untagged guard fails as missing-guard) on itself or an ancestor, or its full path is in PUBLIC_ROUTE_PATHS (src/app/public-routes.ts); redirects are exempt and every lazily loaded child table is passed to the route-gates spec. Fix: add data: { [RouteDataKeys.Permission]: PermissionKeys.<Key> } or, for a page every visitor may open, the public path. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.

Every action element (a <dga-button>; a <button> with any event binding, a submit button or a typeless one in a submitting form; a role=button element with an event binding; any element binding (click) or (confirm), such as a dialog host) in features/**/*.html and in the inline templates of features/**/*.ts carries *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (on itself, on an ancestor element, or [hasPermission] on an <ng-template> wrapper) or an explicit data-public-action for an action every visitor may take. Fix: add the directive with a generated key, or data-public-action. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md.
The kernel never names a module; modules are discovered from the host's ProjectReferences and every name is derived from assembly names (ADR-003, ADR-004).
Public kernel types are a contract with every module; add members, never rename, remove or change a signature without a migration of every module.
